title: Ineluctably
html_source:
“This episode contains practically no action.Nothing happens, and yet in following the trail of Stephen’s thoughts, as he idles on the Dublin strand, we encounter a diversity of experience as exciting as any tale of adventure in ‘the land of Phenomenon’ (Gilbert, S. James Joyce Ulysses, p109).

Stephen is stuck between the abstract and the body, he can’t stop sensory perception – a conflict elucidated by Marxist critical theory:

“McGee uses the Marxist notion that art mediates between the material and social world on one hand and the realm of the ideal on the other to explain that Joyce’s Ulysses mediates "between bodily social existence and aesthetic form” by disclosing the reltionship between the two. The body is explored or even rediscovered through linguistic mediation; conversely, language is shown to be invested with the imaginary value of bodily sensation" (Murfin. A companion to James Joyce Ulysses, ed. M Norris, p215).
